subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept an install-only `plugins install --agent` surface now, or require the full per-agent plugin lifecycle and security contract before this PR can merge?
rationale: The patch changes executable plugin install scope, persisted install identity, and user-facing CLI behavior in a way that affects compatibility and plugin trust boundaries; automation cannot safely choose that product/security contract.

options.title: Require full scoped lifecycle first
options.body: Keep this PR blocked until install, uninstall, update, inspect, doctor, discovery, activation, tests, docs, and proof all use one canonical agent scope.

options.title: Land install-only intentionally
options.body: Maintainers may accept a narrower install-record feature while explicitly documenting that runtime activation remains global and follow-up work owns the rest.

options.title: Pause or replace the PR
options.body: Close or pause this branch if the desired contract is broad enough that a fresh design-led implementation would be cleaner.

recommendation.title: Require full scoped lifecycle first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR blocked until install, uninstall, update, inspect, doctor, discovery, activation, tests, docs, and proof all use one canonical agent scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places this owner closest to the current install/uninstall implementation and compatibility-sensitive plugin lifecycle files.
